instruction: On budget.com, look up rental vehicles available at Boston Logan Intl Airport for a one-day rental.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated budget.com, entered Boston Logan Intl Airport as pickup location, adjusted dates multiple times, submitted search, reached vehicles page, attempted sorting. Encountered captcha and page unresponsive issues during the process.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate budget.com, fill location picker with airport name, adjust date fields, submit search form, reach vehicle results page, interact with sort dropdown, handle captcha dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task required 3 strict checks (URL pattern, date/location HTML parsing with exact whitespace, sort xpath). Model reached vehicles page and changed sort but evaluator's strict format matching on dates and location text failed.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to search + location verification only. Model demonstrated it can enter Boston Logan as pickup location and reach vehicles page. Removes sort and strict date requirements. Checks that the reservation page shows Boston Logan / BOS as the pickup location.
metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for rental cars at Boston Logan on budget.com for a one-day rental. Custom getter extracts URL and checks for Boston Logan / BOS text in accessibility tree. Metric gives 0.5 for reaching reservation page, 0.5 for correct pickup location shown.

scoring_breakdown.location_match: 0.5 - Page shows Boston Logan or BOS as pickup location

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts URL from accessibility tree and checks for 'Boston Logan' (case-insensitive) and 'BOS' (word boundary) presence, which are valid indicators of the correct pickup location.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('url_pattern') without wrapping in expected.get('rules').
Partial credit scoring (0.5 URL + 0.5 location) is reasonable for this two-aspect verification.

Coverage gap: Instruction mentions 'one-day rental' but evaluator does not verify rental duration. This is acknowledged in metadata as an intentional simplification, but it means the evaluator cannot fully verify the instruction.
The 'location' key in expected rules is unused by the metric - the location check is hardcoded in the getter rather than parameterized. Functionally correct but poor design.
Getter URL regex requires characters between :// and budget.com, which works for www.budget.com but could theoretically miss edge cases.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a check for rental duration (e.g., verify dates show a one-day span) to fully cover the instruction requirements.
Use the expected.get('location') value in the metric rather than hardcoding the location check in the getter, for better parameterization.
Simplify getter URL regex to r'https?://[^\s]*budget\.com[^\s]*' to avoid potential edge cases with the character class.
